answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network requires each identity to solve memory-hard graph challenges keyed by a symmetric cipher. An attacker must dedicate physical RAM bandwidth per identity, preventing one machine from hosting thousands of fake agents. Sustaining this live river of memory lookups deepens the latency canyon between native hardware and emulated runtimes. However, this protocol penalizes low-memory edge devices and cannot stop adversaries commanding distributed botnets.
